title: Powers of an endomorphism induced by a natural transport
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be categories, $G:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ an endofunctor, $C:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a functor and $t:C\Rightarrow C\circ G$ a natural transformation, meaning a family $t_A:C(A)\to C(GA)$ satisfying $C(Gf)\circ t_A=t_B\circ C(f)$ for every $f:A\to B$. Write $G^0=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$ and use the usual associative identifications of iterated functor composition. Let $(K,\varphi)$ be a $G$-algebra as in [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]: $K\in\mathcal A$ and $\varphi:GK\to K$ is an arbitrary morphism, with no invertibility condition. For $m\geq1$ define
$$\varphi^{[m]}=\varphi\circ G(\varphi)\circ\cdots\circ G^{m-1}(\varphi):G^mK\to K,\qquad t_K^{[m]}=t_{G^{m-1}K}\circ\cdots\circ t_K:C(K)\to C(G^mK).$$
Then the endomorphism $F=C(\varphi)\circ t_K$ of $C(K)$ satisfies
$$F^m=C(\varphi^{[m]})\circ t_K^{[m]}\qquad(m\geq1).$$
No invertibility of $t$ or $\varphi$ is required.

proof.text:
Use the arbitrary-structure-map clause of [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category], so $\varphi:GK\to K$ need not be invertible. Abbreviate $u_m=\varphi^{[m]}:G^mK\to K$ and $v_m=t_K^{[m]}:C(K)\to C(G^mK)$. The displayed composites in the statement give $u_1=\varphi$, $v_1=t_K$ and, by applying $G$ to each factor and regrouping,
$$u_{m+1}=\varphi\circ G(u_m),\qquad v_{m+1}=t_{G^mK}\circ v_m.$$
Here $G(u_m):G^{m+1}K\to GK$ and $t_{G^mK}:C(G^mK)\to C(G^{m+1}K)$, so both recursions have the required types. These equalities use only functoriality and associativity, with the fixed iterated-composition identifications of the statement.

proof.text:
The induction assertion is $F^m=C(u_m)\circ v_m$ for positive integers $m$. Its base $m=1$ is $F=C(\varphi)\circ t_K$, exactly the definition of $F$. For the successor calculation, substitute the morphism $f=u_m:G^mK\to K$ in the naturality equation assumed for $t$. With its source object $G^mK$ and target object $K$, that equation reads
$$t_K\circ C(u_m)=C(G(u_m))\circ t_{G^mK}.$$
Both sides are morphisms $C(G^mK)\to C(GK)$. Thus the naturality used here is an explicit instance of the hypothesis, not an additional comparison theorem.

source.place: Last proof sentence on Frobenius endomorphisms: base case and the naturality square at the iterated structure map.

proof.text:
Assume $F^m=C(u_m)\circ v_m$ for some $m\geq1$. In the endomorphism monoid of $C(K)$, the definition of powers gives $F^{m+1}=F\circ F^m$. Substitute the induction hypothesis and then the naturality equation of Step 2:
$$\begin{aligned}
F^{m+1}&=C(\varphi)\circ t_K\circ C(u_m)\circ v_m\\
&=C(\varphi)\circ C(G(u_m))\circ t_{G^mK}\circ v_m\\
&=C(\varphi\circ G(u_m))\circ(t_{G^mK}\circ v_m)\\
&=C(u_{m+1})\circ v_{m+1}.
\end{aligned}$$
The third equality is the composition law for the functor $C$ and associativity; the last uses the two recursions of Step 1. Induction proves the required formula for every $m\geq1$. No cancellation or inverse occurs, so this also proves the assertion for noninvertible $t$ and $\varphi$.
